context: Your first evening in town: a small family restaurant with a counter, a handwritten menu and no English. Today: getting seated, ordering and paying.

phrases.note: Staff will ask {何名様|なんめいさま}ですか. Holding up fingers helps too.

phrases.jp: おすすめは{何|なん}ですか。

phrases.note: Point at the menu or the plastic food display. Works everywhere.

phrases.jp: お{会計|かいけい}お{願|ねが}いします。
これ、めっちゃおいしい！
phrases.note: めっちゃ (super) comes from Kansai but young people use it everywhere.

dialogue_setting: At the counter of a small set-meal restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: いらっしゃいませ！{何名様|なんめいさま}ですか。

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: カウンター{席|せき}へどうぞ。お{決|き}まりでしたら、お{呼|よ}びください。
dialogue.en: Please take a counter seat. Call me when you've decided.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: すみません、おすすめは{何|なん}ですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, what do you recommend?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: {今日|きょう}は{焼|や}き{魚|ざかな}{定食|ていしょく}がおすすめです。
dialogue.en: Today the grilled fish set meal is our recommendation.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、それをお{願|ねが}いします。

kanji.where: On menus and boards outside small restaurants: a main dish with rice, miso soup and pickles. Usually the cheapest filling option at lunch.
kanji.related: Related: {大盛|おおも}り large portion, {日替|ひが}わり daily special.

tip.title: Rice refills and the call button
tip.body: Many places refill rice for free: ask ご{飯|はん}のおかわり、できますか. If the table has a call button, press it instead of calling out; otherwise a clear すみません！ with a raised hand is normal. You pay at the register by the door, and there's no tipping.

challenge.prompt: You've finished eating. Catch the staff's attention and ask for the bill.
challenge.hint: to call staff = すみません, bill = お{会計|かいけい}
challenge.model_answer: すみません、お{会計|かいけい}お{願|ねが}いします。
